questions.q: What is the oldest University in the United States?
questions.hint: Founded in 1636 in Cambridge, Massachusetts—it starts with the letter H.

questions.q: Which US athlete has won the most Olympic gold medals ever?
questions.hint: He is a legendary American Olympic swimmer who won 23 Olympic gold medals.

questions.hint: He was the 16th President of the United States during the Civil War.
questions.pageExcerpt: "3. Which US president issued the Emancipation Proclamation? — Abraham Lincoln"

questions.q: The Tet Offensive was a turning point in which war?
questions.hint: This conflict took place in Southeast Asia during the 1960s and 1970s.

questions.q: What happened on October 28, 1929, also known as Black Monday?
options: End of the American Civil War.
Signing of the Declaration of Independence.
questions.hint: The stock market crash on this date triggered a severe worldwide economic crisis in the 1930s.
questions.pageExcerpt: "5. What happened on October 28, 1929, also known as Black Monday? — Start of the Great Depression."

quizzes.title: Trapped in a Video Game: Chapters 3 & 4

questions.q: At the start of Chapter 3, what finally reminds Jesse Rigsby that he has a weapon while a man-eating praying mantis is charging at him?
options: He tries curling into a tiny ball while screaming, and the blaster strapped to his arm gets in the way.
Eric shouts instructions to him from the top of the snow-covered boulders.
The robot army sergeant appears and orders him to fire his weapon.
He trips over a floating mechanical grenade attachment in the snow.
questions.hint: Think about Jesse's 'last trick' when the praying mantis is almost on top of him.
questions.pageExcerpt: "With the creature almost on top of me, I pulled out my last trick: screaming while curling into a tiny ball. But even that didn’t work because the stupid blaster kept getting in the... Oh. Wait. The blaster."
questions.clue: The energy weapon strapped to Jesse's arm in the video game

questions.q: True or False: When Jesse shoots the invisible wall in the Rocky Mountains at full blast from two feet away, the wall shatters and opens an escape path.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the ball of light when it hits the invisible brick wall.
questions.pageExcerpt: "Owwwwww! I punched an invisible brick wall. I shook my hand, then tried blasting it. Nothing. Maybe full blast? I charged the blaster and shot the invisible wall from two feet away. The ball of light absorbed into the wall and disappeared."
questions.clue: Impossible to see, like the barrier blocking Jesse from walking back

questions.q: Match each person, place, or detail from Chapter 3 with its accurate description:

pairs.right: Boy from Middlefield, Ohio who imagines his resistance lasted 10 seconds
rightVariants: Boy from Middlefield, Ohio who imagines his resistance lasted 10 seconds
Kid from Middlefield, Ohio who jokes about his funeral inside a video game
Narrator who wishes he had brought his inhaler while running from aliens
Reluctant player chased through the snowy mountains by giant insects

pairs.right: Unseen boundary in the Rocky Mountains that absorbs blaster shots
rightVariants: Unseen boundary in the Rocky Mountains that absorbs blaster shots
Clear barrier that makes a CLUNK sound when Jesse hits his head or fist
Hidden game border that prevents Jesse from walking back the way he came
Impenetrable transparent wall that juts in without warning near the pines

pairs.right: Jesse's failed guess that praying mantis aliens only see things that move
rightVariants: Jesse's failed guess that praying mantis aliens only see things that move
Mistaken idea that standing completely still would keep the aliens from spotting him
Bad theory disproven immediately when the mantis stands up and squawks
Dinosaur comparison Jesse makes right before the alien spots him anyway

pairs.right: Dead-end area with 50-foot walls where Jesse is cornered by the horde
rightVariants: Dead-end area with 50-foot walls where Jesse is cornered by the horde
Enclosed mountain basin where three aliens pour in for every one vaporized
50-foot-high dead end where Eric rescues Jesse from the top of the cliff
Box canyon where praying mantises stampede until Jesse is 15 feet from doom

distractorVariants: Secret underground tunnel Jesse digs in the snow to escape the mountains
Flying hoverboard Jesse finds hidden behind the pine trees
Friendly alien guide who hands Jesse a map of Middlefield, Ohio
Force-field shield that bounces praying mantises back over the cliff
questions.hint: Recall Jesse's imagined funeral, the unseen boundary he hits, his dinosaur comparison, and the 50-foot dead end.
questions.pageExcerpt: "Here lies Jesse Rigsby of Middlefield, Ohio... After five minutes of walking along an invisible wall in the Rocky Mountains... I stayed very still because maybe praying mantis aliens are like T. rexes, where they can only see things that move... Suddenly, the canyon opened up into a big bowl with 50-foot walls. A dead end."
questions.clue: Deep gorge with high walls where Jesse gets trapped at a dead end

questions.q: While running from the six-legged praying mantises, what item does Jesse really wish he had brought with him—and blames Eric for not mentioning in his text?
questions.hint: Jesse jokes about who would ever think to bring this breathing item to a video game.
questions.pageExcerpt: "I found the path and continued running and blasting wildly behind me, really wishing I’d brought my inhaler. But who brings an inhaler to a video game? I blamed Eric. He should have texted, 'Come over. You’re not going to believe this. Maybe bring your inhaler.'"
questions.clue: Breathing device Jesse wishes he had while sprinting through the mountains

questions.q: What tip does Eric Conrad shout down from the cliff that allows Jesse to vaporize a whole group of aliens with a single shot?
options: "Aim only for their six insect legs!"
"Bounce your shots off the invisible wall!"
"Hide inside the pine trees until they pass!"
questions.hint: Think about how Jesse changes his blaster shot from single blasts to a more powerful shot.
questions.pageExcerpt: "'Glad you’re having fun! Try charging up to full blast!' I did what he said. It worked! I got a whole group with one blast. Eric and I worked together on clearing the entire canyon of aliens."
questions.clue: To make the aliens disappear into a blinding flash of light

questions.q: True or False: At the end of Chapter 3, the creature that sneaks up behind Eric and shoots him is a regular green praying mantis.
questions.hint: Remember how Jesse describes the sneaky creature's color, number of legs, and weapon arm.
questions.pageTitle: Chapter 3 — Page 21 (The Ambush on the Cliff)
questions.pageExcerpt: "Sneaking up behind Eric was a jet-black creature that looked a little more alien than praying mantis with five legs and one long blaster arm. 'Eric!' He looked at me. The alien lowered its blaster... The alien pulled the trigger, and my best friend in the whole world vaporized before my eyes."
questions.clue: One of the last three remaining aliens trailing behind the main group

rightVariants: When Jesse first met Eric while Eric's parents unloaded a moving truck
The school year when Eric moved in and Jesse became his best friend
Age when Jesse believed Eric was 'getting close' to learning how to fly
Six years ago when the two boys first started their friendship

rightVariants: Hat whose tail Eric spun with his hand in the front yard to try to fly

The first time I saw him, his parents were unloading the moving truck, while Eric ran back and forth in the front yard wearing a coonskin cap and spinning the tail with his hand... We never learned how to fly, but we did learn how to jump pretty high off of homemade bike ramps and start fires with magnifying glasses and scare each other during backyard sleepovers..."

questions.q: According to Eric in Chapter 4, how did he unlock 'Reality Mode' and get sucked into the video game?
options: He finally beat the game earlier that afternoon, and a screen at the end of the credits asked if he wanted to try 'Reality Mode'.
He entered a secret cheat code he found printed inside the game manual.
He connected two broken blasters together to his television screen.
He downloaded an experimental update from the alien base portal.
questions.hint: Eric explains what popped up on the screen at the end of the game's credits after he beat it.
questions.pageExcerpt: "Eric shrugged. 'I think so. Earlier this afternoon, I finally beat the game. At the end of the credits, a screen came up that said I’d unlocked something called "Reality Mode" and asked if I wanted to try it. When I said yes, I got sucked in like you did.'"
questions.clue: The ending list of names after beating a game where Reality Mode appeared

questions.q: How does Eric earn the mechanical grenade-launcher attachment in Chapter 4?
options: He lures 50+ aliens to a tiny cave opening they can't fit through and vaporizes the whole group in one charged shot.
He finds it inside a locked supply crate next to the HOME portal.
He takes it from the robot army sergeant after finishing the tutorial.
He shoots down the tops of two big pine trees where it was hidden.
questions.hint: Remember why Eric dragged Jesse into a small cave and fired a small blast into the snow.
questions.pageExcerpt: "'Wait,' Eric said as he dragged me into a small cave. 'Watch this.' He shot a small blast into the snow to get the aliens’ attention. Soon, one came over, then two, then 50 or more. They were all trying to reach us, but they were all too big to fit into the tiny opening. Finally, Eric charged his blaster and vaporized the whole group in one shot. After the blinding light, we heard a chime and saw a mechanical part float over the snow. Eric woo-hooed, ran over, and clipped it onto his blaster. 'Now I can launch grenades!'"

questions.q: True or False: Eric tells Jesse that they are permanently trapped inside the game until they defeat every single level in the entire world.
questions.hint: Think about what Eric says appears at the end of each level that lets players return to real life.
questions.pageTitle: Chapter 4 — Page 27 (Portals at the End of Each Level)
questions.pageExcerpt: "'Oh, we’re not stuck,' Eric said as he started walking... 'At the end of each level, there’s a portal that takes you back to real life. I finished two levels, then decided to go back and tell you about it.'"
questions.clue: Glowing doorway at the end of a level that can send players back to real life

rightVariants: Shelter with a tiny opening too small for the 50+ giant aliens to fit through

options: He knew nothing he could say would convince Jesse to come in because Jesse is 'such a baby.'

THUNK THUNK. Eric took out the alien that had shot him earlier. '...so I just had to let you discover it for yourself.'"
questions.clue: To persuade someone to believe or do something

A glitch caused by the invisible brick wall in the Rocky Mountains.

quizzes.readerHtml:
CHAPTER 3: Blast Blast Squawk!

[Page 15] I did the thing you’re supposed to do when a man-eating praying mantis starts charging at you: I screamed a squeaky scream. “AHHHHHHH!” The praying mantis did not slow down. I tried adding running to the mix. “AHHH...” THUD. “AHHH...” THUD. “AHHH...” THUD.

Running over snow-covered rocks with a blaster strapped to your arm is harder than it looks. With the creature almost on top of me, I pulled out my last trick: screaming while curling into a tiny ball. But even that didn’t work because the stupid blaster kept getting in the... Oh. Wait. The blaster.

[Page 16] At the last second, I closed my eyes, reached up and squeezed my left hand. The blaster recoiled, and I heard a shriek. I opened my eyes to see the praying mantis disappear into a ball of light.

Wow. I almost died. Inside of a video game. I imagined the funeral. “Here lies Jesse Rigsby of Middlefield, Ohio. He was tragically taken from us by a giant praying mantis while trying to save a video game world from fake aliens. He bravely led the resistance, which lasted for all of 10 seconds.”

I looked around me. Snow and boulders everywhere, with a path leading deeper into the mountains ahead of me. No thanks. I turned and started walking back to find a way out of this mess. I got exactly five steps before... CLUNK. I hit something and fell backward into the snow. Confused, I picked myself up and tried again. CLUNK. I got up and inspected the spot further. It was open air, no different from anything else around me. I tried to put my fist through it. CLUNK.

[Page 17] Owwwwww! I punched an invisible brick wall. I shook my hand, then tried blasting it. Nothing. Maybe full blast? I charged the blaster and shot the invisible wall from two feet away. The ball of light absorbed into the wall and disappeared. I sighed, put my hand against the wall, and started walking to find an opening.

After five minutes of walking along an invisible wall in the Rocky Mountains (not exactly an activity I thought I’d be doing when I woke up), I heard a noise to my left. Clickclickclick. I slowly turned. Through several pine trees, I could see two praying mantises scuttling back and forth, guarding the main path. Gulp. I slowed down and crept quieter to keep from alerting the... CLUNK.

The invisible wall had jutted in with no warning, and I clunked my head against it. One of the creatures turned. I stayed very still because maybe praying mantis aliens are like T. rexes, where they can only see things that move. SQUAAAAWWWWWWWWWWWWWK!

[Page 18] Nope! Bad theory. Bad, bad, bad theory. The creature that had heard me was now standing on its back legs and making a creepy squawking noise while the other one charged. I ran as fast as my little legs would take me. While climbing over boulders and dodging trees, I kept reaching back and wildly blasting at my attackers. Blast-blast-blast-SQUAWK!

It may not surprise you to learn that the creatures with six nimble insect legs were quickly gaining on the off-balance person who did not post a mile time to be proud of in gym class the previous week. Blast-blast-blast-SHRIEEEEEEEEEEEK! Got one! Unfortunately, I had no time to celebrate because the mantis I had vaporized was replaced with another one who’d heard his battle cry. And then another.

I found the path and continued running and blasting wildly behind me, really wishing I’d brought my inhaler. But who brings an inhaler to a video game? I blamed Eric. He should have texted, “Come over. You’re not [Page 19] going to believe this. Maybe bring your inhaler.” Or perhaps, “Come over UNLESS YOU DON’T WANT TO GET CHASED BY MAN-EATING ALIENS THROUGH THE MOUNTAINS.” You know, just to give me a choice.

As I ran and blasted, the terrain on either side of the path grew higher and higher until I found myself running through the bottom of a canyon. Praying mantises were now jumping into the canyon behind me, joining their brothers in a stampede of death. Suddenly, the canyon opened up into a big bowl with 50-foot walls. A dead end.

I ran to the end, turned around, and started blasting. By this time, I was getting better at picking them off, but it was too late. For every alien I vaporized, three more would pour through the canyon opening. The horde got closer and closer: 30 yards away. Then 20. Then just 15 feet. I continued shooting while closing my eyes, preparing to meet my end.

Then a chorus of shrieks. I opened my eyes to see the blinding light of five aliens getting vaporized at once. Before I could figure out what was happening, the wave behind them also disappeared. “Jesse!”

[Page 20] I looked up. Eric. Eric Conrad, looking exactly like a superhero, was blasting away from the top of the cliff. “Hey, buddy! What do you think?” “THIS IS THE WORST! GET ME OUT OF HERE!” I screamed.

[Page 21] “Glad you’re having fun! Try charging up to full blast!” I did what he said. It worked! I got a whole group with one blast. Eric and I worked together on clearing the entire canyon of aliens.

After five minutes, the only group left was three stragglers coming in through the opening. I turned around to watch Eric line up the shot, and that’s when I saw it. Sneaking up behind Eric was a jet-black creature that looked a little more alien than praying mantis with five legs and one long blaster arm. “Eric!” He looked at me. The alien lowered its blaster. “WATCH OU...” The alien pulled the trigger, and my best friend in the whole world vaporized before my eyes.

CHAPTER 4: Reality Mode

[Page 23] Eric had been my best friend since first grade. The first time I saw him, his parents were unloading the moving truck, while Eric ran back and forth in the front yard wearing a coonskin cap and spinning the tail with his hand. I finally went over to ask him what he was doing. He said that he was trying to fly and was “getting close.” I believed him because I was in first grade, and all first-graders believe that they’re this close to flying. I decided right then to stick with this strange flying child and learn his ways.

And for the next six years, I did stick with him. Through everything. We never learned how to fly, but we did learn how to jump pretty high off of homemade bike ramps and start fires with magnifying glasses and scare each other during backyard sleepovers until we were afraid to go into the house to pee. And now he was gone.

[Page 26] “Come on,” Eric said as he started walking down the path. “Hey,” I caught up with him. “You going to explain what this is all about?” “Oh yeah!” Eric’s eyes lit up. “Isn’t this the greatest thing in the world? Can you believe it?” “No! Definitely not! Is this real?”

Eric shrugged. “I think so. Earlier this afternoon, I finally beat the game. At the end of the credits, a screen came up that said I’d unlocked something called ‘Reality Mode’ and asked if I wanted to try it. When I said yes, I got sucked in like you did.”

[Page 26–27] “Wait,” Eric said as he dragged me into a small cave. “Watch this.” He shot a small blast into the snow to get the aliens’ attention. Soon, one came over, then two, then 50 or more. They were all trying to reach us, but they were all too big to fit into the tiny opening. Finally, Eric charged his blaster and vaporized the whole group in one shot. After the blinding light, we heard a chime and saw a mechanical part float over the snow. Eric woo-hooed, ran over, and clipped it onto his blaster. “Now I can launch grenades!” he shouted.

THUNK THUNK. I waited patiently while Eric shot grenades at two big trees. The grenades detonated in a flash of light, and the tops of the trees disappeared. Eric nodded approvingly. “At the end of each level, there’s a portal that takes you back to real life. I finished two levels, then decided to go back and tell you about it. I knew that nothing I [Page 28] could say would convince you to come in here because you’re such a baby...” THUNK THUNK. Eric took out the alien that had shot him earlier. “...so I just had to let you discover it for yourself.”

“...And then this army guy starts yelling at me and making me do all this weird stuff...” “That was the tutorial,” Eric interrupted. “The tutorial. It’s there to teach you how to play the game. That sergeant’s not real—he’s like a robot that’s only programmed to do one thing.”

[Page 29] “Whatever. And now everything’s trying to kill us, AND I HAVE MATH HOMEWORK THAT’S DUE ON MONDAY!” ... “I’ll let you shoot a grenade.” I glared some more. Eric unclipped his grenade launcher and put it on my arm. “Try it.” I squeezed. Two grenades THUNK THUNKed out of my arm and vaporized a praying mantis that I didn’t see sneaking up next to us. “Wasn’t that great?!” Eric exclaimed. It was. It was very great. “Hmf.”

[Page 30–31] “Come on. We’ve got an alien base to defeat,” Eric said as he ran ahead... “This is it,” Eric said, as he led me through a final door inside the alien base. Inside, we found a room with three glowing portals. One said “REPLAY,” another said “HOME,” and the last said “LEVEL 2.”

“All right, I’ll let you keep going,” I said as I took a step toward the HOME portal. “Wait.” Eric grabbed me. “Don’t you want to keep going?” “No. I told you I want to go home.” “One more level.” “Nope.” “The next one is in Hawaii.” “Sorry.” “They have jet packs.” I squinted at him. “Jet paaaaaacks.” Finally, I rolled my eyes. “One more level.” “WOO-HOO!” We walked past the HOME portal into LEVEL 2. It was the worst decision of my life.
